newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian budget to return to lower house Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: Italian budget to return to lower house Dec 16.

text.p: Italy's tough 1997 budget will return to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on December 16 after its passage through the Senate (upper house), parliamentary party leaders said on Wednesday.
The party leaders in the Chamber expect the passage of the bill to take until December 23. Under Italian law, an identical text must be approved by both houses of parliament.
The package, which aims to slice 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit ($40.7 billion), is due to be debated in the full Senate from December 10.
It was passed by the Chamber last month but requires a further reading there because of changes introduced in the Senate, where the package is now at the committee stage.

When the budget returns to the Chamber, deputies will consider a controversial "Euro-tax" designed to help Italy become a founder member of European monetary union. Last month's budget debate in the Chamber did not include the Euro-tax. ($1=1,533 lire)
